---
title: "Settings"
---
The user must set the model settings in the `settings.toml` configuration file.

Besides the necessary/ required setttings one can set:

- input in regard to the computational side of FIAT (e.g. chunking, number of threads etc),
    - see this [page](computation.qmd)
- optional/ additional input that is not necessary or more data specific,
    - see this [page](optional.qmd)

### Basic input
This section pertains to all input that is vital for running a FIAT model.

These inputs/ entries are listed in the table down below with more detailed information per entry underneath the table.

::: {.callout-note}
File paths in the settings can be relative to the settings.toml file or absolute.
:::

| Entry                          | Type    | Required | Default         |
|:-------------------------------|---------|----------|-----------------|
| [type](#type)                  | string  | Yes      |                 |
| [output_dir](#output_dir)      | string  | No       | output          |
| **[hazard]**                   |         |          |                 |
| [file](#hazard)                | string  | Yes      |                 |
| **[[exposure]]** (geom)        |         |          |                 |
| [file](#exposure)              | string  | Yes      |                 |
| **[exposure.variables]** (geom) |        |          |                 |
| [vulnerability](#exposure)     | string  | Yes      |                 |
| **[exposure]** (grid)          |         |          |                 |
| [file](#exposure)              | string  | Yes      |                 |
| **[vulnerability]**            |         |          |                 |
| [file](#vulnerability)         | string  | Yes      |                 |
: Most basic settings file input {#tbl-toml .hover}

#### type

- `type`: The type of model. Choice between 'geom' and 'grid'.

#### output_dir

- `output_dir`: The path to the output directory.

#### [hazard]

- `file`: The file path to the [hazard file](../data/hazard.qmd).

#### [exposure]

For the geometry model (`type = "geom"`), every geometry file gets its own `[[exposure]]` entry:

- `file`: The path to the exposure vector file (recommended to be within the [exposure directory](../data/index.qmd)) with the [assets](../data/exposure/geometry.qmd).
- `variables.vulnerability`: The name of the (single) [vulnerability dataset](../data/vulnerability.qmd#linking-exposure-to-datasets) linked to this file. The `[exposure.variables]` table of every entry is required.

For the grid model (`type = "grid"`), there is a single `[exposure]` section:

- `file`: The path to the [exposure raster file](../data/exposure/grid.qmd) (recommended to be within the [exposure directory](../data/index.qmd)).
The vulnerability dataset(s) of the layers are set per variable in the `[[exposure.variables]]` entries, see [grid exposure data](../data/exposure/grid.qmd#layers).

#### [vulnerability]

- `file`: The path to the vulnerability NetCDF file within the [vulnerability directory](../data/index.qmd) that contains the [vulnerability datasets](../data/vulnerability.qmd). Only one vulnerability file is allowed.

::: {.callout-note}
The calculation method is set per vulnerability dataset (the `method` of the `[[vulnerability.variables]]` settings), see [methods](../data/vulnerability.qmd#methods). There is no global `method` setting.
:::

The variables (datasets, bands and layers) of the vulnerability, hazard and (gridded) exposure data can be further specified with `[[vulnerability.variables]]`, `[[hazard.variables]]` and `[[exposure.variables]]` entries, see the [optional input](optional.qmd#variables).

### Example

An example of settings file for running a geometry model is given below:

```toml
type = "geom"
risk = false
output_dir = "output"

[hazard]
file = "hazard/event_map.nc"

[[exposure]]
file = "exposure/buildings.fgb"

[exposure.variables]
vulnerability = "default"

[vulnerability]
file = "vulnerability/curves.nc"
```

An example of settings file for running a grid model with combined depth and duration vulnerability datasets is given below:

```toml
type = "grid"
risk = false
output_dir = "output"

[hazard]
file = "hazard/event_map_duration.nc"

[[hazard.variables]]
name = "depth"
type = "water_depth"

[[hazard.variables]]
name = "duration"
type = "flood_duration"

[exposure]
file = "exposure/spatial.nc"

[[exposure.variables]]
name = "exposure2"
type = "default"
fn_curve = "struct_2"
vulnerability = ["direct", "indirect"]

[vulnerability]
file = "vulnerability/curves_multi.nc"

[[vulnerability.variables]]
name = "direct"
method = "flood.depth_duration"
types = { depth_direct = "water_depth" }

[[vulnerability.variables]]
name = "indirect"
method = "flood.depth_duration"
types = { days_indirect = "flood_duration" }
```
